title: Obscure Song Selection Occasionally Ruins an Otherwise Fun Game
body: Fun game, but obscure song selections often ruin the fun and leave me and my friends frustrated. The point of the game is to recognize the song from the isolated instrument tracks. Right? So, when you’ve never heard the song before, what’s the point? I’m not trying to be mean - I know you put in a lot of work and seem to be a one-man operation, and you’ve done great. This app would be one of my favorite creations ever, except that the songs we’re guessing are often obscure songs like “Modern Talking - Brother Louie”, which defeats the point of the game and kills the fun. Other songs from 1986 that would be fun, yet still present a challenge, to try and guess just from the drums: Hip to Be Square Danger Zone Two of Hearts Everybody Have Fun Tonight Papa Don’t Preach Lady in Red Higher Love Nasty So, please pick less obscure songs! The challenge should not lie in how familiar or unfamiliar the song is, the fun lies in guessing the song from the isolated tracks. When you don’t know the song, it kills the fun.

title: Please learn what Par means
body: BIGGEST ISSUE is that whatever way they calculate Par makes ZERO SENSE so it doesn’t help you as a hint and it also messes up your stats page. Par is supposed to be the expected AVERAGE tries needed to succeed. Bandle 899 is a Par 2 meaning 50% of people should get it right by guess 2. Problem is, only 3% got it in 1, 8% in 2, 12% in 3, and 15% in 4. Through 4 tries only 38% of people got it right, it’s par should be 5. I’ve played 38 games and there’s more than a handful that are like that. What’s the point of doing all the work to make a stats page that breaks down your answers into over/on/under par and even lists them by the songs decade if half of those scores are judged against nonsense pars? Other than that it’s a pretty fun game. It’s free and you get one new game a day. If you miss one you can play it the next day still which is nice. Wish they gave you more plays per day though.

title: A fun concept that keeps me coming back, could use more attention to detail sometimes
body: I love nerding out about music, so I’ve played this game since I first heard about it months ago. When it’s at its best, it’s really fun and I love hearing the parts of songs I love split up. It’s not always perfect, though. The biggest issue is typically the recreations of certain parts using sub-par VSTs, especially for strings, horns and other more exotic instruments. Sometimes they even get the names wrong for some instruments (which can drive music majors like myself and my friends a bit crazy—I’ll never forget the time they called steel drums a marimba). The bonus questions can have some really fun facts (when they’re correct, of course). I’ve also bought a couple song packs and really appreciate the extra effort put into those stems (I was especially surprised to hear some actual vocals)! All in all, with maybe a bit more people putting together and editing everything for consistency, this can definitely be 5-star game.

title: Best Music Game Going
body: This is an extraordinary wordle-type game for music lovers. I have been playing for a couple weeks, and I can confidently say that it has everything you could ask for in a music guessing game. The songs are popular enough that I am rarely left not knowing or hearing the song before, yet it still offers an interesting and thought provoking challenge by playing individual instruments. The hints are also a nice touch to get a better idea of possibilities for what the song may be. It’s always a good time playing this game with a groups of friends. My only gripe with the game is that you are limited to 1 game per day. There are 3 packs of 5 songs for which you can watch videos to play, then you must buy packs to have access to the rest of the archive. I would watch videos ‘til the cows come home if it meant i could get more games per day. Maybe players could get their first play of the day, then they can watch videos to get more plays, and put a cap of 3 extra songs per day from watching videos. Or something like that. If the ad revenue makes sense to do this, then i think it would be a great addition. Whoever created this game, you rule! Keep up the great work.

But I like how this one has its own app instead of just a website, and I like how it shows you the percent of players who got it on which ever number they guessed it on. Really cements in the difficulty of some of them.

title: What I’ve been missing
body: Been wanting a game like this since Spotify killed Heardle. While the overall look and design could use some work the potential is there! The game itself is great. I like the split up parts and the average (par) system. The bonus game to answer questions about the song also tickles that music lover part of my brain that always wants to know more. So far I haven’t had a song I’d consider obscure or unknown. Keep up the great work! Hope this app sticks around cause I really enjoy it!
